title: try_send Full/Closed distinction: correct and worth defending
description: The old code used .is_err() to handle both TrySendError::Full and TrySendError::Closed identically (silent break). The new code explicitly splits them: Full → warn + break (stalled consumer, operator should know), Closed → silent break (client disconnected, expected). This split is correct engineering: Full is a signal that something is wrong with the SSE consumer and an operator needs to investigate; Closed is a normal lifecycle event. A future contributor might suggest 'simplifying' back to .is_err() to reduce code, which would silently suppress the stall warning and make ops-level debugging impossible. The verbosity is load-bearing.
